column5: This word shows position, it does not tell how the snail moved. => This word shows position. It does not tell how the snail moved.
Most adverbs add -ly, but some change first. => Most adjectives add -ly to make an adverb, but some change first.
For words ending in y, change the y to i first. => For most words ending in y, change the y to i first.
-le to -ly rule too broad (sole, whole) => for many words
A comma follows a fronted adverbial phrase. => A comma usually follows a fronted adverbial phrase.
They are written in brackets, so => They are often written in brackets, so
hint said "first sentence" but the keyed sentence is the last option => no position named
until dark taught as a subordinate clause (it has no verb) => row now Citra sat until I came, answer until I came
It starts with a conjunction. => It often starts with a conjunction.
Only the first spoken word and names need capital letters. => Capital letters go on the first spoken word and on names, not on every word.
Reported speech moves one tense back (no exception) => usually, 5 items: .013 .014 .017 .023 .701
Words that point to the speaking moment need to change. => Words that point to the speaking moment usually need to change.
Do becomes lived. => Do you live becomes he lived.
Reported speech changes the tense and the pronouns. => Reported speech often changes the tense and the pronouns.
why "Nothing was changed" false, I became she => Here and yesterday were not changed
Reported speech changes tense, place and time words. => Reported speech often changes tense, place and time words.
rule "i before e except after c" stated with no limit (weird, their, science) => when the sound is ee, 3 items: .002 .022 .803
Two complete sentences need a full stop between them or a joining word. => Two complete sentences usually need a full stop between them or a joining word.
Check the verbs again, one of them is wrong. => Check the verbs again. One of them is wrong.
option D (one girl) was also correct, prompt never said how many girls => prompt now says several girls and several teachers
With she, the verb needs an s, so it should be She goes to school every day. => With she, a present tense verb usually ends in s, so it should be She goes to school every day.
Was makes this a metaphor false (He was tall) => says hope was a candle
expl named children who are not in the item => anyone who enters
Watching is an unfriendly word. => Here, watching feels unfriendly.
why said no events, the poster announces one => no characters or plot
would gives advice too broad => If I were you, I would
Modal verbs show how likely or necessary something is. => Modal verbs can show how likely or necessary something is.
p, b, m "usually take im-" false (unpleasant, unbroken, unmarried) => many words
Words starting with l take il- false (unlucky, dislike) => many words
The shun sound is not spelt -shun at the end of English words. => The shun sound is not usually spelt -shun at the end of English words.
Start with -less and -ful, they are opposites. => Start with -less and -ful. They are opposites.
Impossible, irregular, illegal and incorrect all mean not. => Impossible, irregular, illegal and incorrect all start with a prefix meaning not.
doubling rule too broad (repeating, relaxing) => one consonant after one vowel, usually
false in en-GB for travelling, cancelling => usually
un- also reverses (unwrap) => Here, un- means not
shyly, slyly => usually
They means more than two people, so it is unclear. => They could mean both boys or other people, so it is unclear.
fewer coins so I need less money made no sense => so I have less money
why cited chocolate on the plate, the text says fingers
accepted answer list held the wrong form a adult => removed
past of sing is sang => Sung is a form of sing
There are two books: there does not tell a place here
The third is a place (there). => The third goes with is (there is).
index printed out of order while the hint says alphabetical => cacti before camels
exact figure is an estimate => hundreds of years
Green algae grows in their fur and helps them hide. => Green algae grow in their fur and help them hide.
prompt named a paragraph the child could not see => paragraph added
why named "my", which is not in the sentence
expl cited "you", which is not in the leaflet => commands such as Join
model gave 2 reasons while rubric and planning ask for 3 => third reason added
Instructions use a command verb like "add" in the present form, not the past tense. => Instructions use a command verb like "add", not the past tense.
Stage directions are written in brackets and tell the actors what to do. => Stage directions are usually written in brackets and tell the actors what to do.
The rule is i before e, except after c. => The rule is i before e, except after c, when the sound is ee.
always (got broken is also passive) => usually
The subject of a passive sentence is the thing that matters most. => The subject of a passive sentence is often the thing the writer wants to focus on.
Then it sold at the market is good English (bread sells), so option D was defensible => carried, in the prompt, option and explanation
Extra information goes in the middle of a sentence. => Extra information often goes in the middle of a sentence.
They surround the extra information. => They should surround the extra information.
Words ending in -ly take no hyphen is false (family-friendly, friendly-looking) => adverbs ending in -ly, why and hint
relative clauses do not begin with a conjunction => This subordinate clause
Long, flowing sentences feel slow, not fast. => This long, flowing sentence feels slow, not fast.
rule ignored semicolons in lists, taught in .008 of the same file => limited to semicolons that join clauses, why and hint
colon rule made usually, 3 items: .003 .011 .020
hint implied a clause after the gap always takes a semicolon, .007 teaches a colon before a clause => Here
Remember: was correct here but "Pack:" marked wrong in .011 for the same reason => Remember this:
semicolon then capital: I also takes a capital
If I was you is common informal English => prompt says formal, also .701 and .805
and speech needs a capital letter. => and speech needs speech marks and a capital letter.
Two complete sentences need a full stop or a joining word. => Two complete sentences usually need a full stop or a joining word.
hints and explanation spoke of "nicest furniture", which is not in the item => lovely
A narrator tells a made-up story. => A narrator tells a story, often a made-up one.
prompt asks for at least eight sentences, model had five => three sentences added
Children is formal and kids is informal. => Children is the standard word and kids is informal.
A fable always ends with a moral. => A fable usually ends with a moral.
A fable has talking animals and a moral, not clues and footprints. => A fable usually has talking animals and a moral, not clues and footprints.
Poems are written in lines and stanzas. => Poems are usually written in lines and stanzas.
tiles answer "Poems are divided into stanzas" too broad => Many poems, with hint and explanation
keyed sentence mixed past and future => If Leo falls off, he might break a leg
Rapids are in the middle of a river, so this is not about an ending. => Rapids are not the end of a river, so this is not about an ending.
The cat stays across the room. => The cat stays in the room.
hint pointed at "the night being wide awake", which is not in the item
This repeats the problem and does not link to solutions. => This is a fact about bags and does not link to solutions.
Breath is only visible in cold air. => Breath is usually visible only in cold air.
The title page only gives the book's title and author. => The title page gives the book's title and author, not the pages for a topic.
by degrees means gradually => Shade from trees can cool a school
sole, whole => many words
why named the wrong letter place: the extra h in wheather is after the w
rule limited to the ee sound, .021 of spelling-homonyms
why said the missing a comes after the s, in plesant it is the a after the e that is missing
Whose asks who something belongs to. => Whose shows who something belongs to.
after a short vowel we write dge false (village, cabbage, message) => in a short word, usually; .001 and .006
tch after a short vowel stated with no exception (much, such, rich, which) => usually, key option and explanation
boxing, fixing => usually
why on hapiness explained the wrong mistake, the fault is the missing p
argument, truly => usually
Words ending in le lose the e. => Many words ending in le lose the e.
After c the pair is written ei false (science, ancient) => the ee sound, why, 2 hints and explanation
some coasts have one tide a day, the Sun also pulls => in most places, mainly
a formal letter also has a problem and a solution (.002 asks for it) => a plot with
A news report states facts and does not begin with a question. => A news report states facts and does not usually begin with a question.
It is written in the past tense. => It is mostly written in the past tense.
Stage directions go in brackets. => Stage directions usually go in brackets.
explanation claimed sight and smell, the sentence uses touch and sound
An opening phrase needs one comma. => An opening phrase usually takes one comma.
.017 teaches must as almost certain, will as certain => hint and explanation agree now
and then read as one phrase, the word then is the option named
After if we use the present tense false for If I had wings => in a real possibility, hint and explanation
One is where the club moved to, one is the old place. => One is where the club moved to. The other is the old place.
When words join to describe a noun, they are linked with hyphens: => When words join to describe a noun, they are often linked with hyphens:
adverbs describe verbs, => adverbs often describe verbs,
A semicolon joins two main clauses and cannot be used before a list. => A semicolon can join two main clauses, but it cannot be used before a list.
Semicolons also need a full clause after them. => Here, semicolons also need a full clause after them.
mixed conditional (If I had eaten, I would not be) is above Cambridge Stage 6 level, kept at d=4, a teacher may want to drop it
